主要内容: Robert Murray, a prominent figure in the coal industry, has long been known for his support of union miners, a legacy that has become part of his story. However, his company, Murray Energy Corp, has faced significant financial challenges, leading to its bankruptcy filing. The company, which has been in operation for six decades, is now burdened with over $2.7 billion in debt. As part of a proposed restructuring, Murray, who is 79 years old, will no longer serve as the chief executive officer of the company he founded. A new entity will take over the company's assets, while the $8 billion in pension and health-care obligations to miners will be abandoned. This marks the end of an era for Murray, who has been a key player in the coal industry for many years.
